speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific nature of the pain and swelling in your right ring finger, and when did these symptoms first begin? Are there any other symptoms, such as fever, redness, or stiffness, that you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of a traumatic injury and the rapid onset of swelling and pain, is there any visible deformity, discoloration, or an open wound at the injury site? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and ESR. Can you tell me if you have a fever, or if the swelling has spread up the finger toward the knuckle?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Distal Interphalangeal Joint Volar Plate or Extensor Tendon Injury)

The mention of Pyelonephritis is incorrect; that is a kidney infection unrelated to your finger injury. Your inability to flex the distal joint after catching your finger on a jersey is classic for a Mallet Finger. Please apply a rigid extension splint to your finger continuously for 6 weeks and return in one week for follow-up.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
